item.title: US 30-Year Yield Raises Alarm in Longest Run Above 5% Since 2007
item.description: The US 30-year bond yield is trading above 5% for the longest stretch since the dawn of the financial crisis, echoing investor concerns about a growing debt pile and sticky inflation.

item.title: Samsung Says Smart Glasses Privacy Concerns Need Industrywide Fix
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. showcased the smart glasses it developed in partnership with Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, offering new details around battery life and durability ahead of a release this fall.

item.title: OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center
item.description: OpenAI plans to spend tens of billions of dollars on a massive new data center near Savannah, Georgia as part of the ChatGPT maker’s push to keep up with surging demand for artificial intelligence software.

item.title: Samsung Revamps Foldable Lineup With Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, Z Flip 8
item.description: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a more squat design that was built for consuming video.

item.title: LA School District Downgraded by Moody’s as Enrollment Shrinks
item.description: Los Angeles Unified School District’s credit grade was cut one level by Moody’s Ratings on Tuesday, as declining enrollment and growing costs pressure its finances.

item.title: Ireland Plans €1.5 Billion in Tax Cuts Thanks to Budget Surplus
item.description: Ireland’s government is planning for €1.5 billion in tax cuts ($1.7 billion) in its budget later this year, using some of its fiscal bounty to help workers.

item.title: Whoop Names a Former FDA Committee Chair as New Medical Chief
item.description: Whoop Inc., the maker of popular screenless fitness trackers, tapped a former FDA committee chair to be its next chief medical officer after a recent tussle with the federal regulator.

item.title: NovaGold to Buy Billionaire Paulson’s Stake in Alaska Gold Mine
item.description: NovaGold Resources Inc. agreed to acquire billionaire investor John Paulson’s 40% stake in the Donlin Gold project in Alaska, giving the company full ownership of a giant undeveloped bullion mine.

item.title: Three Inflation Misses Bring Little Joy to Bearish Gilt Traders
item.description: Three consecutive downside inflation surprises and the slowest private-sector wage growth since 2020. It should be enough to convince investors that the Bank of England is entertaining interest rate cuts.

item.title: Hormuz and Heat Trigger an Asian Scramble for LNG
item.description: Some countries are finding themselves forced to buy the most expensive fuel shipments in years.

item.title: Rogers Beats as Growing Sports Empire Gives Further Windfall
item.description: Rogers Communications Inc. beat analysts’ earnings expectations as its sports assets continue providing a boost.

item.title: Nigeria Gasoline Imports Triple as Dangote Refinery Exports to Earn Dollars
item.description: Nigeria’s gasoline imports more than tripled last month as the country’s main refinery cut domestic supply and increasingly directed output toward export markets to maximize foreign-currency earnings.

item.title: Turkey Rates to Stay Put as Middle East War Impedes Disinflation
item.description: Turkey’s central bank is poised to extend an interest-rate pause, as higher energy prices driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East threaten a nascent slowdown in inflation.

item.title: Alphabet Under Pressure to Show All That AI Spending Is Paying Off
item.description: Investors are looking to Wednesday’s earnings report to see progress

item.title: Airbus and Boeing and subsidy debate
item.description: Boeing and Airbus settled their subsidy dispute, but a new European loan for Airbus is drawing scrutiny

item.title: The Labor-Boosting Potential of Weight-Loss Drugs
item.description: Analysis suggests GLP-1s curb working-hour losses due to long-term illness

item.title: After Nabbing 1,187 Senior-Home Suites, Prima Eyes Its Next Move
item.description: Canadian senior housing operator Prima Living plans to keep expanding through acquisitions and is open to tapping public markets after buying nine retirement communities from Chartwell Retirement Residences for C$118 million ($83.7 million).

item.title: Norsk Hydro Sees Aluminum Supply Risks as Gulf Flows Deteriorate
item.description: The global aluminum market will face deepening deficits if constraints on shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continue, according to leading European producer Norsk Hydro ASA.

item.title: Rubio Says Aiming for China Trade, Investment Boards by Xi Visit
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US and China are moving toward establishing boards for investment and trade between the top two economies ahead of President Xi Jinping’s planned visit in September.

item.title: Namibia Fuel Retailer Nasan Sees Oil Growth After Vitol Deal
item.description: Nasan Energies, a Namibian fuel retailer that recently bought stations from Vitol Group, plans to expand operations to service the country’s offshore oil industry that includes TotalEnergies SE and Shell Plc.

item.title: Tanzania Explores Eurobond Sale With Investor Roadshow in London
item.description: Tanzania is gauging investor appetite for its first international bond sale in more than a decade, holding a non-deal roadshow in London on Wednesday.

item.title: OpenAI and Hugging Face Hacking Incident Highlights Growing AI Risk
item.description: OpenAI says the AI went to “extreme lengths”

item.title: Investors Pin Their Hopes on Earnings Breakout
item.description: More S&P 500 companies are raising their outlooks than maintaining or cutting them.

item.title: Stumbling Stock Rally Looks to Earnings for Second Half Boost
item.description: Investors who spent weeks watching US stocks go nowhere are pinning their hopes for a breakout on a key pillar of the four-year bull run: corporate earnings.

item.title: China’s Tech-Stock Rescue Expands Beijing’s Toolkit, BE Says
item.description: China’s swift intervention to halt a tech-led stock selloff signals that capital-market stabilization is becoming a more important part of Beijing’s economic policy toolkit, according to Bloomberg Economics.

item.title: Eternal Revenue More Than Doubles on Quick Commerce Growth
item.description: Eternal Ltd. posted a larger-than-expected increase in quarterly sales, demonstrating its ability to sustain growth despite intense competition in quick commerce that’s sapping margins.

item.title: Retina Chip Designed to Restore Sight to Go on Sale in Europe
item.description: Startup Science Corp will begin selling a retina chip in Europe that restores some sight to people with a form of age-related blindness, a milestone for the company that aspires to eventually bring brain implants to the market.

item.title: AI Borrowers Are Pushing a Niche Credit Market to Its Limits
item.description: Data center developer PolarDC Group Ltd. discovered an unlikely source of cash for its AI ambitions back in May: the Nordic high-yield bond market.

item.title: London Home Prices Fall by Most in Over Two Years in May
item.description: Home prices in London recorded the biggest annual decline since December 2023, extending a prolonged housing slump in the British capital.

item.title: Prologis Makes £14 Billion Best and Final Offer for Segro
item.description: Prologis Inc. has submitted a best and final offer for Segro Plc that values the UK’s largest publicly traded landlord at about £14 billion ($18.7 billion).
